summary: Backend perf-cache validation (iteration 231). 12/12 tests passed. Verified cache speedup, data integrity, and cache invalidation across POST/PUT/DELETE on /api/operations. No regressions on /api/health, /api/vehicles, /api/stats.

minor.issue: Returns 404 — endpoint mentioned in review_request does not exist. /api/stats exists instead. Verify which is the intended path for the dashboard.

action_items: Clarify whether /api/dashboard/stats should be wired (currently 404) or if frontend uses /api/stats. Not blocking the perf-cache change.
critical_code_review_comments: perf_cache.py uses module-level in-process dict — correct for single-instance deployment but will not work if backend is scaled horizontally (each pod has its own cache). Acceptable given current k8s setup but document this assumption.

_CACHE has no max-size bound — for high-cardinality cache keys (ops_list keyed by combined filters) this could grow indefinitely if many distinct filter combinations are queried. Consider an LRU cap or per-namespace size limit.

_invalidate_ops_caches() in routes_extended.py drops 4 namespaces but does NOT drop 'vehicle_customer_lookup' — if operation create/update changes vehicle linkage, vehicle_customer_lookup stays stale up to 15s. Review whether ops mutations affect vehicle->customer mapping (likely no, but worth confirming).

TTL of 10s for /operations vs 15s for partner_fin_map — a customer creating an op and refreshing /customers within ~15s may see stale balances because partner_fin_map is invalidated correctly only if ops mutation paths call _invalidate_ops_caches. Confirmed this is wired in POST/PUT/DELETE/bulk-delete/confirm-payment.

Cache invalidation depends on every mutation route calling _invalidate_ops_caches(). Any future endpoint that writes to operations or journal_entries must remember to invalidate. Consider centralising in a service layer or using a DB-trigger / version-counter approach.
test_credentials: Not needed — public backend APIs tested directly.
seed_data_creation: Created 2 transient test operations with notes prefix 'TEST_perf_*' — both deleted in test teardown / by delete test. No residual data expected.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Perf-cache backend behaviour validated. Cache speedup measured: /customers 5.7x, /suppliers 2.7x. Cache invalidation verified for POST/PUT/DELETE on /api/operations. Note: operation entity uses 'notes' (not 'description') as the free-text field. /api/dashboard/stats returns 404 — use /api/stats. Next testing agent can focus on frontend perf validation if requested.
